accessibilityAttributes.description:
Defines additional accessibility attributes on different areas of the component.

The accessibilityAttributes object has the following field:

 - **growingButton**: `growingButton.name`, `growingButton.description`.

 The accessibility attributes support the following values:

- **name**: Defines the accessible ARIA name of the growing button.
Accepts any string.

- **description**: Defines the accessible ARIA description of the growing button.
Accepts any string.

 **Note:** The `accessibilityAttributes` property is in an experimental state and is a subject to change.

**Note:** Available since [v2.13.0](https://github.com/UI5/webcomponents/releases/tag/v2.13.0) of **@ui5/webcomponents**.

accessibleDescription.description:
Defines the accessible description of the component.

**Note:** Available since [v2.5.0](https://github.com/UI5/webcomponents/releases/tag/v2.5.0) of **@ui5/webcomponents**.

accessibleDescriptionRef.description:
Defines the IDs of the elements that describe the component.

**Note:** Available since [v2.5.0](https://github.com/UI5/webcomponents/releases/tag/v2.5.0) of **@ui5/webcomponents**.

accessibleName.description: Defines the accessible name of the component.

accessibleNameRef.description: Defines the IDs of the elements that label the component.

accessibleRole.description: Defines the accessible role of the component.

children.description:
Defines the items of the component.

**Note:** Use `ListItemStandard`, `ListItemCustom`, and `ListItemGroup` for the intended design.

__Supported Node Type/s:__ `Array<ListItemBase | ListItemGroup>`
children.x-typescriptType: string | number | boolean | ReactElement<any, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Array<ReactNode>

className.description:
CSS Class Name which will be appended to the most outer element of a component.
Use this prop carefully, overwriting CSS rules might break the component.

growing.description:
Defines whether the component will have growing capability either by pressing a `More` button,
or via user scroll. In both cases `load-more` event is fired.

**Restrictions:** `growing="Scroll"` is not supported for Internet Explorer,
on IE the component will fallback to `growing="Button"`.

growingButtonText.description:
Defines the text that will be displayed inside the growing button.

**Note:** If not specified a built-in text will be displayed.

**Note:** This property takes effect if the `growing` property is set to the `Button`.

**Note:** Available since [v1.24](https://github.com/UI5/webcomponents/releases/tag/v1.24) of **@ui5/webcomponents**.

header.description:
Defines the component header.

**Note:** When `header` is set, the
`headerText` property is ignored.

__Note:__ The content of the prop will be rendered into a [<slot>](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/slot) by assigning the respective [slot](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/slot) attribute (`slot="header"`).
Since you can't change the DOM order of slots when declaring them within a prop, it might prove beneficial to manually mount them as part of the component's children, especially when facing problems with the reading order of screen readers.

__Note:__ When passing a custom React component to this prop, you have to make sure your component reads the `slot` prop and appends it to the most outer element of your component.
Learn more about it [here](https://ui5.github.io/webcomponents-react/v2/?path=/docs/knowledge-base-handling-slots--docs).

__Supported Node Type/s:__ `Array<HTMLElement>`
header.x-typescriptType: false | ReactElement<any, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReducedReactNode> | ReactElement<any, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Array<InternalUI5WCSlotsNode>

headerText.description:
Defines the component header text.

**Note:** If `header` is set this property is ignored.

indent.description: Determines whether the component is indented.

loading.description: Defines if the component would display a loading indicator over the list.

loadingDelay.description: Defines the delay in milliseconds, after which the loading indicator will show up for this component.

noDataText.description: Defines the text that is displayed when the component contains no items.

onItemClick.description:
Fired when an item is activated, unless the item's `type` property
is set to `Inactive`.

**Note**: This event is not triggered by interactions with selection components such as the checkboxes and radio buttons,
associated with non-default `selectionMode` values, or if any other **interactive** component
(such as a button or input) within the list item is directly clicked.

**Note:** Call `event.preventDefault()` inside the handler of this event to prevent its default action/s.

| cancelable | bubbles |
| :--------: | :-----: |
| ✅|✅|

onItemClose.description:
Fired when the `Close` button of any item is clicked

**Note:** This event is only applicable to list items that can be closed (such as notification list items),
not to be confused with `item-delete`.

| cancelable | bubbles |
| :--------: | :-----: |
| ❌|✅|

onItemDelete.description:
Fired when the Delete button of any item is pressed.

**Note:** A Delete button is displayed on each item,
when the component `selectionMode` property is set to `Delete`.

| cancelable | bubbles |
| :--------: | :-----: |
| ❌|✅|

onItemToggle.description:
Fired when the `Toggle` button of any item is clicked.

**Note:** This event is only applicable to list items that can be toggled (such as notification group list items).

| cancelable | bubbles |
| :--------: | :-----: |
| ❌|✅|

onLoadMore.description:
Fired when the user scrolls to the bottom of the list.

**Note:** The event is fired when the `growing='Scroll'` property is enabled.

| cancelable | bubbles |
| :--------: | :-----: |
| ❌|✅|

onMove.description:
Fired when a movable list item is dropped onto a drop target.

**Note:** `move` event is fired only if there was a preceding `move-over` with prevented default action.

| cancelable | bubbles |
| :--------: | :-----: |
| ❌|✅|

onMoveOver.description:
Fired when a movable list item is moved over a potential drop target during a dragging operation.

If the new position is valid, prevent the default action of the event using `preventDefault()`.

**Note:** Call `event.preventDefault()` inside the handler of this event to prevent its default action/s.

**Note:** Available since [v2.0.0](https://github.com/UI5/webcomponents/releases/tag/v2.0.0) of **@ui5/webcomponents**.

| cancelable | bubbles |
| :--------: | :-----: |
| ✅|✅|

onSelectionChange.description:
Fired when selection is changed by user interaction
in `Single`, `SingleStart`, `SingleEnd` and `Multiple` selection modes.

**Note:** Call `event.preventDefault()` inside the handler of this event to prevent its default action/s.

| cancelable | bubbles |
| :--------: | :-----: |
| ✅|✅|

selectionMode.description: Defines the selection mode of the component.

separators.description: Defines the item separator style that is used.

stickyHeader.description:
Indicates whether the List header is sticky or not.
If stickyHeader is set to true, then whenever you scroll the content or
the application, the header of the list will be always visible.

**Note:** Available since [v2.19.0](https://github.com/UI5/webcomponents/releases/tag/v2.19.0) of **@ui5/webcomponents**.

style.description:
Element style which will be appended to the most outer element of a component.
Use this prop carefully, some css properties might break the component.

waitForDefine.description:
Defines whether the component should wait for the underlying custom element of the web component to be defined. This can be useful, for example, for using instance methods when mounting the component.

__Note:__ This adds a rendering cycle to your component.
